items.title: Record the grounded module decomposition and the reuse-not-rebuild and cut-FTS decisions
items.context: 4 core + 2 handler modules under packages/main with one-way inward coupling (usage-ledger style); reuse dev-memory capture, decision-doc-promotion digest pattern, activity-log appender; cut full-text search for v1.
items.userSees: The doc contains a module-decomposition section listing the new core/ and handlers/ modules, a reuse section naming dev-memory.ts / decision-doc-promotion.ts / activity-log.ts, and an explicit cut-FTS statement.

happy.desc: Doc contains a module-decomposition section header (H2 or H3) -> grep -i finds module.decomposition or module.structure heading; WHY: verifies the section exists

Module-decomposition section lists the four core modules (experience-layer-types, learning-store, finding-signals, experience-hint-loader) -> grep finds all four module names; WHY: completeness of decomposition
Module-decomposition section lists the two handler modules (learning, playbook) -> grep finds both handler module names; WHY: completeness of decomposition
Doc describes one-way inward coupling (handler -> core -> types direction) -> grep finds one-way or inward coupling language; WHY: architectural constraint is a key decision
Doc contains a reuse section naming dev-memory.ts, decision-doc-promotion.ts, and activity-log.ts -> grep finds all three filenames; WHY: reuse-not-rebuild is a core decision
Doc contains explicit cut-FTS statement (cutting full-text search for v1) -> grep -i finds cut.*FTS or cut.*full.text.search; WHY: explicit scope cut is a key decision

edge.desc: The three reuse files (dev-memory.ts, decision-doc-promotion.ts, activity-log.ts) actually exist in the codebase -> find . -name dev-memory.ts etc. each returns at least one result; WHY: reuse claims must reference real code
Doc mentions packages/main as the location for new modules -> grep finds packages/main; WHY: module location claim must be grounded

adversarial.desc: Doc does not claim FTS is included or planned for v1 (no contradictory language) -> grep for phrases like full-text search.*v1.*include or FTS.*enabled finds no contradictions; WHY: cut-FTS must be unambiguous
No module is listed in both core/ and handlers/ (no category confusion) -> reviewer confirms each module appears in exactly one category; WHY: decomposition must be clean

items.title: Document the three determinism guardrails and the back-compat rules
items.context: Guardrails: audit-only finding fields excluded from gates; finding-signals read via stable finding accessor (store.readFindings) not raw findings.json; hints excluded from reviewer promptHash domain. Back-compat: dismissReasonType optional; flat underscore command names.
items.userSees: The doc has a determinism-guardrails section enumerating all three guardrails and a back-compat note (optional dismissReasonType, flat underscore commands).

happy.desc: Doc contains a determinism-guardrails section header -> grep -i finds determinism.guardrail heading; WHY: verifies the section exists

Guardrail 1: doc states audit-only finding fields (signatureTag, resolutionType, dismissReasonType, evidenceStrength) are excluded from gate reads -> grep finds audit-only fields excluded from gates; WHY: first guardrail completeness
Guardrail 2: doc states finding-signals read via store.readFindings not raw findings.json -> grep finds store.readFindings and findings.json exclusion; WHY: second guardrail completeness
Guardrail 3: doc states hints excluded from promptHash domain -> grep finds promptHash and hints exclusion; WHY: third guardrail completeness
Doc contains back-compat note stating dismissReasonType is optional -> grep finds dismissReasonType.*optional; WHY: back-compat requirement
Doc contains back-compat note about flat underscore command names -> grep finds underscore command names or flat.*command; WHY: back-compat requirement

edge.desc: store.readFindings actually exists as a method in the codebase -> grep -r readFindings packages/main/src/ finds at least one match; WHY: code-grounded claim must reference real API
promptHash is a real concept in the codebase -> grep -r promptHash packages/main/src/ finds at least one match; WHY: guardrail references must be grounded in real code
All three guardrails are enumerated (numbered or bulleted list of exactly three) -> reviewer confirms three distinct guardrail items; WHY: prevents missing or duplicate guardrails

adversarial.desc: Doc does not state that audit-only fields ARE used in gates (no contradictory language) -> grep for audit.*field.*gate.*use or gate.*read.*signatureTag finds no affirmative gate-use claims; WHY: guardrail 1 must not be contradicted

Doc does not claim hints affect determinism or promptHash (no contradictory language) -> reviewer confirms no statement says hints are included in hash computation; WHY: guardrail 3 must not be undermined

items.title: Document the phased roadmap with first story = verifiable finding-signals slice, and include accurate code anchors
items.context: Phased rollout (Phase 1a first, then 1b/1.5/2/3/4); first story is the finding-signals vertical slice proven by an unchanged currentMaterialHash() test; code anchors are real file paths.
items.userSees: The doc has a roadmap section naming Phase 1a as the first story and an appendix of real code anchors; no Co-Authored-By trailer anywhere.

happy.desc: Doc contains a roadmap section header -> grep -i finds roadmap or phased.rollout heading; WHY: verifies the section exists
Roadmap names Phase 1a as the first story -> grep finds Phase.1a as first; WHY: phase ordering is a key plan decision
Phase 1a is described as the verifiable finding-signals slice -> grep finds finding-signals in the Phase 1a description; WHY: first-story scope must be clear
Doc references currentMaterialHash() test as the proof that Phase 1a does not break determinism -> grep finds currentMaterialHash; WHY: verifiability claim is central
Doc contains a code-anchor appendix section -> grep finds code.anchor or appendix heading; WHY: appendix is a required section

Code-anchor appendix lists real file paths (types.ts, finding.ts, store.ts, advisory.ts, dev-memory.ts, runtime-artifact-registry.ts, story-review.ts, activity-log.ts, decision-doc-promotion.ts) -> grep finds at least 7 of these filenames; WHY: completeness of anchors

Every code-anchor file path listed in the appendix resolves to a real file in the repo -> verifier script checks each path with fs.existsSync; WHY: prevents dangling references that mislead implementers
Doc contains no Co-Authored-By trailer anywhere -> grep -i Co-Authored-By returns no matches; WHY: explicit prohibition per user standing requirement

edge.desc: Roadmap lists all phases in order (1a, 1b, 1.5, digest-extract, 2, 3, 4) -> reviewer confirms at least 5 distinct phases mentioned; WHY: phased rollout must be complete
currentMaterialHash exists as a real function in the codebase -> grep -r currentMaterialHash packages/main/src/ finds at least one match; WHY: test reference must be grounded
runtime-artifact-registry.ts exists in the codebase -> find . -name runtime-artifact-registry.ts returns at least one result; WHY: code anchor must resolve

adversarial.desc: No code-anchor path points to a file that was deleted or renamed -> verifier checks every anchored path and reports zero FAIL; WHY: stale anchors are worse than missing ones because they appear valid

Doc does not contain Co-Authored-By in any form (case-insensitive, including partial matches like co-authored) -> grep -i co-authored-by finds zero matches in the doc; WHY: trailer prohibition is absolute
No phase is listed out of order or duplicated -> reviewer confirms monotonic phase numbering and no repeated phase labels; WHY: roadmap ordering must be unambiguous
